cover.title: StockVisible
cover.oneliner: See the demand that stock-outs hide, then decide what to reorder within budget — with forecasts whose reliability is proven.
in_short: 20.2% of the hours from 6:00 to 22:00 are out of stock in the training data: observed sales underestimate demand.
Three screens: Verify (the evidence), Understand (one product's demand), Buy (basket within budget, validated then exported).
ML engine chosen on validation only, frozen, then evaluated a single time: MAE 3.2% lower than B1 on the final test, with a negative bias shown on screen.
Real FreshRetailNet-50K data (CC BY 4.0), normalised: no currency unit, no data from Senegal.

problem: When a product is out of stock, the till records zero sales. That zero is not an absence of customers: observed sales underestimate demand, and a manager who reorders on that basis reorders too little, which sustains the stock-outs.
In the data used (500 real store × product series of fresh produce), 20.2% of the hours from 6:00 to 22:00 are out of stock over the training period.

Target user: the manager or purchasing lead of a fresh-produce outlet, who must decide every day what to reorder with a limited budget. No interview or pilot with a manager has taken place yet: this need is a working assumption, not a need validated in the field.
data: FreshRetailNet-50K, Dingdong-Inc, CC BY 4.0 licence, revision 08c1fab7f9257bc73679d415d65d644165d351d4 (arXiv:2505.16319).
Deterministic subset of 500 series (seed 42), filtered without modifying any value. Sales normalised by the provider: no currency unit.

Real / simulated separation: the application's reference data is this real benchmark. No synthetic FCFA scenario was built; costs, lot sizes and stock levels are assumptions entered by the user. The only synthetic files are the test fixtures, named *_SYNTHETIQUE.csv.
The dataset's official “eval” file is not versioned and has never been used to evaluate a model.
method: B0: median of sales in the same time slot, stock-outs included. B1: the same median restricted to hours declared available, with abstention. ML: quantile gradient boosting (scikit-learn) on strictly past features.

Rolling day-ahead (J+1) hourly forecasts, hours when the product was available, the same hours for all three models. On the final test, opened a single time, the ML's error is 3.2% lower than B1's (5.4% on validation). It under-forecasts (negative bias, close to B0): this is shown on screen, and it is why the basket does not use it.
The masked-data test is a reconstruction / fidelity test: it measures the fidelity of the reconstruction, not the real lost demand. It is not proof of recovering real demand.
architecture: app.py: router of the three screens (st.navigation). No model is trained at run time: the Verify screen reads engine_freeze.json, logs/final_test_result.json and logs/interval_calibration.json.
Interface: Streamlit 1.64, Plotly charts, design system in design-system/MASTER.md. Data contract and decision log: docs/data-contract.md.
limits: Real Chinese data (Dingdong), normalised: no currency unit, no FCFA, no data from Senegal.
Costs, lot sizes and stock levels are entered assumptions: the dataset contains none.
Demand lost during a stock-out is estimated, never observed. The masked-data test measures the fidelity of the reconstruction, not the real lost demand.
Modest ML gain (3.2% on the test) and negative bias; the basket uses B1.
The rows of the test period were read before the split (data quality check) and are public in the repository; they were not used for any model decision.
Render free tier: cold start observed at about 2 minutes after 15 minutes of inactivity.
No interview or pilot with a manager: the user need remains a working assumption.
rai: No LLM and no external AI API in the application: the engine is a tabular model competing against two simple rules.
Visible abstention: when no comparable period exists, B1 predicts nothing and the screen says so; the hours stay empty, never filled by default.

Measured uncertainty: 80% interval around the engine, empirical coverage of 79.5% on validation days never seen during calibration; “interval not calibrated” is shown when support is insufficient. At night the interval is [0, 0]: calibrated but not very informative.

Real / simulated separation: real data flagged as such; costs and stock levels flagged as assumptions; synthetic test files labelled; lost demand always presented as estimated. Limitations shown on screen.
evidence: 20.2% of 6:00–22:00 hours out of stock; problem banner computed from the data; observed sales and estimated demand side by side
Import → visualisation → evidence → budget → basket → validation → export path, local and production, desktop and mobile, zero console errors; export identical to the screen
ML against B0 / B1, rule written before any result, choice on validation only, frozen configuration (SHA-256 fingerprints); final test opened a single time
Reproducible split; anti-leakage through canaries and perturbation; 9 negative controls; dress rehearsal of the final test; GitHub Actions CI
Three screens Verify → Understand → Buy; at most three metrics per screen; computed WCAG AA contrasts
Visible abstention; interval coverage 79.5%; real CC BY 4.0 data, pinned revision; assumptions and synthetic files labelled
ai_usage: In the product: a scikit-learn tabular model, with no LLM and no external AI API. NVIDIA Brev: not used.

To build it: Claude Code (Anthropic) as programming assistant — Claude Sonnet 4.6 for the first commit, Claude Opus 5.5 afterwards; a separate Claude session for the 4 finishing commits of pull request #1; read-only Claude agents for the security audit and a simulated evaluation against the jury grid. Skills: stockvisible-data-contract and dataviz. No MCP server.
The project owner sets the rules and takes the decisions traced in the Git history; every commit carries the corresponding Co-Authored-By line.

Timeline (UTC, Git history): M0 → M10 on 26/09/2026 from 16:03 to 23:29; M11 → M17 on 27/09/2026 from 00:56 to 13:11. The rules on code prepared before the event are those of the official regulations.
roadmap: Pilot with an outlet equipped with a till and stock tracking, with its real costs.
Then a purchase-oriented engine (quantile above the median) chosen on validation and evaluated on the dataset's official “eval” period, never used to evaluate a model.
Choose a licence for the code: no licence file has been added to the repository yet.
pending: Demo script and video (M18): to come.
screens: The problem in one sentence, then the evidence: errors of the ML engine and of the two baselines on validation and on the final test, uncertainty, guarantees, limitations
For one product: hour-by-hour sales, availability, observed sales vs estimated demand per day, B0 / B1 forecasts, abstention; import of a file checked against the data contract
Costs, lots and stock levels entered as assumptions; budget; optimal basket (covered demand, shortfall); validation then CSV / JSON export with provenance
screens_intro: The manager does not need to read the code: the application first shows them the evidence of reliability (Verify screen), then the demand for one product (Understand), then a basket within budget that they validate and export (Buy).
discipline_flow: DATA → TRAIN (60 d) → VALIDATION (15 d) → ENGINE CHOICE → FREEZE → FINAL TEST ONCE ONLY (15 d)
discipline: Chronological split per series, never random.
Selection rule written before any result: the ML is kept only if it beats B1 on validation, otherwise B1 becomes the engine.
Anti-leakage tested: canaries, perturbation of future days, and 9 negative controls (leaks injected on purpose, which the suite must detect).
Two looks at the validation set are declared: the first model was degenerate (it predicted 0 everywhere); it was fixed once, then the configuration was frozen.
architecture_table: Deterministic, verified (SHA-256) subset of the dataset; data contract; safe reading of imported files (CSV / Parquet, size and row caps, no execution of content)
Hourly sales, declared availability, estimated demand
splits.py, baselines.py, features.py, model.py, evaluation.py, selection.py, final_test.py, uncertainty.py
Chronological split, B0 / B1 baselines, strictly past features, ML model, selection on validation, freeze, single final test, empirical interval
Optimal basket within budget, bounded exhaustive enumeration (≤ 3 products), whole lots
Basket validation, CSV / JSON export strictly identical to the screen
tests_note: On a fresh clone, 2 tests are skipped because they need data files that are not versioned (official eval, download cache), with an explicit reason. GitHub Actions CI: ruff, pytest, pip-audit (informational). Free Render instance (512 MB, sleeps after 15 min of inactivity). No secret is needed.
licences: Dependencies: open-source libraries listed in requirements.txt (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, Streamlit, Plotly, pyarrow, pytest, ruff, pip-audit) and package.json (@playwright/test, testing tool only), each under its own licence.
StockVisible code: no licence file has been added to the repository yet; without an explicit licence, rights remain reserved to the author.
chronology: The Git history is authoritative. First commit on 26/09/2026 at 16:03 UTC; data, model, freeze, final test and screens (M0 to M11) committed on 26/09/2026 and overnight until 27/09 at 00:56 UTC; E2E tests, security audit, export, CI, production and finishing work on 27/09/2026.
